aspects.says: A compareAndSet memo keeps one result for every caller but can still run the load more than once.
basis: section:A Memo Written as Check-Then-Compute Loads Twice When Two Threads Arrive Together

aspects.says: Computing eagerly needs no memo but pays, and fails, at startup.
basis: section:A Safe Memo Chooses What It Pays: a Lock, Class Initialisation, or Startup Time
aspects.reason: a choice of design whose cost is startup time and a failed start, which a unit test of one class does not observe; the memo practice requires the lazy form instead

aspects.says: A supplier passed as a factory, as to Collectors.toCollection or ThreadLocal.withInitial, must return a new object per call; one that returns a shared object makes every group or thread share it.
basis: section:A Factory Supplier Must Return a New Object on Every Call

aspects.says: Stream.generate calls the supplier once per element without end, so only a short-circuiting step such as limit ends it.
basis: section:A Factory Supplier Must Return a New Object on Every Call
aspects.reason: a stream that never ends can only be graded by a timeout on a hung call; the page shows the run, and the check would test the timeout rather than the idea

aspects.says: A Supplier runs its body on every get() and keeps no result, so creating it runs nothing and each call can return a new object.
basis: section:A Supplier Runs Its Body on Every get() and Remembers Nothing

aspects.says: A holder class loads once through class initialisation, but a failed initialiser makes every later use throw NoClassDefFoundError until restart.
basis: section:A Safe Memo Chooses What It Pays: a Lock, Class Initialisation, or Startup Time

aspects.says: Objects.requireNonNull(obj, Supplier) and Optional.orElseThrow(Supplier) call the supplier only on the failing path, while the String overload builds its message on every call.
basis: section:The JDK Takes a Supplier Where the Work May Not Be Needed

aspects.says: Double-checked locking with a volatile flag loads once, keeps a null result, and retries after a failed load.
basis: section:A Safe Memo Chooses What It Pays: a Lock, Class Initialisation, or Startup Time

aspects.says: A check-then-compute memo without a lock lets two threads that arrive together both run the load.
basis: section:A Memo Written as Check-Then-Compute Loads Twice When Two Threads Arrive Together

aspects.says: IntSupplier, LongSupplier, DoubleSupplier and BooleanSupplier are separate interfaces, not subtypes of Supplier, and are adapted with a method reference.
basis: section:IntSupplier and Its Siblings Return Primitives and Are Not Suppliers

aspects.says: ThreadLocal.withInitial calls its supplier on each thread's first get() and keeps the result for that thread.
basis: section:A Factory Supplier Must Return a New Object on Every Call
